answer: Plant honeypot tasks whose correct answer is already known, and score any account that confidently returns the planted wrong answer. Cause and effect are short: one such account gets its epoch quota capped, so a farm probing the pool loses reach exactly when it needs volume. A fresh nonce per submission blocks replay, and the trap register is an umber mark on the ledge of every pool, readable before a new identity is admitted, so the inlet for cheap clones narrows with each catch. The cost is one sacrificed trap per farm found, far below the value of the identities it removes.
